claims.text: An optimal range of lattice distortion promotes deformation twinning and strain hardening in high-entropy alloys.
Deformation twinning and strain hardening caused by optimal lattice distortion retain toughness.
Excessive atomic-size mismatch accelerates brittle behavior and causes toughness loss.
The proposed baseline is an equiatomic, single-phase high-entropy alloy with moderate lattice distortion and known toughness characteristics.
Increasing the concentration of an element with a substantially different atomic radius will incrementally increase lattice distortion.
The tests will be conducted at moderate temperatures and strain rates while secondary-phase formation is excluded.
The extent of lattice distortion mediates deformation-twin formation and strain distribution.
Moderate lattice distortion activates deformation twinning.
Deformation twinning enhances ductility and toughness by delaying crack propagation.
Excessive lattice distortion localizes strain and promotes brittle fracture.
Strain localization and brittle fracture caused by excessive distortion reduce overall toughness.
A small-to-moderate increase in lattice distortion relative to the baseline will increase twinning activity.
A small-to-moderate increase in lattice distortion relative to the baseline will improve toughness.
Extreme increases in lattice distortion will decrease toughness and cause earlier crack initiation.
The proposed behavior is limited to single-phase, equiatomic high-entropy alloys under ordinary engineering mechanical-loading conditions.
The proposed behavior may not hold in multiphase alloys or at extreme temperatures or strain rates because other mechanisms may dominate.
Failure to observe both increased twin density and improved toughness at moderate distortion, or failure to observe a toughness decline at high distortion, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Changing the concentration of one element away from an equiatomic baseline generally produces non-equiatomic samples, whereas the stated boundary restricts the hypothesis to equiatomic alloys.
